solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Flawless screen getting smashed

parts.note: to screen a programme is to air it, broadcast it
smashed and tight are both slang for drunk

explanation.surface: A display screen has been broken and is no longer perfect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting' is only a link; 'smashed' looks like an anagram signal but means drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: An argument with no holes or weak points is called watertight or airtight, i.e. faultless.

clue.text: Attack from rising Turkish submarine

indicators.note: rising says the hidden letters are read backwards
from here means taken out of the run of letters spanning the two words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An attack launched by a Turkish submarine as it surfaces.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft named no hiding signal; 'from' is it, so it is added as the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: A surprise attack by people lying in wait is a form of assault.

clue.text: It's left for all to see in lodge

indicators.note: in places the certificate letter inside the word for lodge

parts.note: to lodge is to reside, to live somewhere
U is the British film certificate for universal viewing, suitable for all

explanation.surface: Something has been left in a lodge, open for anyone to see.
explanation.definitionFit: What remains after the rest is removed, a leftover, is what's left.

clue.text: Understanding clue ending badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters of the two words are jumbled

explanation.surface: A solver understands that a clue's ending is poor.
explanation.definitionFit: Tolerance and lenience toward others' faults is a sympathetic understanding.

clue.text: Someone must pay teacher with drink and bread

parts.note: a head teacher runs a school
to swill is to drink greedily
a roll is a small loaf of bread

explanation.surface: A teacher must foot the bill for drinks and bread.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom says people will be punished or sacked, meaning someone will pay for a failure.

clue.text: Reverence for Muslims sadly rejected by leaders in America?

indicators.note: rejected means sent back, so the word for sadly is read backwards

parts.note: alas is an exclamation meaning sadly, unfortunately
the leading letters of America are A and M

explanation.surface: A Muslim form of respect is sadly turned down by American leaders.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaders' is plural: the first two letters of America are taken.
explanation.definitionFit: A salaam is a low bow with the hand to the forehead, a respectful greeting in Muslim countries.

clue.text: Opener from admiral meeting boat?

indicators.note: opener from means the first letter of the following word

parts.note: a hoy is a small coastal sailing vessel

explanation.surface: An admiral's first words when hailing another boat.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a sailor's greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafarer's call hailing another vessel is the opening word of such an encounter.

clue.text: Sweet, posh lass detained in a jail briefly

indicators.note: detained in says the girl is held inside the jail
briefly says the last letter is cut off

parts.note: nick is British slang for prison
gel is how an upper-class Briton might say girl

explanation.surface: A well-to-do, charming girl has been briefly locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nick' is British slang for prison; 'gel' mimics an upper-class pronunciation of girl.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone sweet and innocent is described as like a heavenly being.

clue.text: To sit in liquid surrounding trailer is jolly!

indicators.note: surrounding says the soldier's word goes around the trailer

parts.note: Jolly is old naval slang for a Royal Marine
an ad (advertisement) is a trailer, as for a film

explanation.surface: Sitting in a bath around a trailer park is great fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat steeped in a seasoned liquid before cooking does exactly this.

clue.text: Coach player wanting change? Not half

indicators.note: not half says only the first half of the word is kept, the rest dropped

parts.note: a busker is a street musician hoping passers-by will give coins

explanation.surface: A sports coach hints that a player wants a transfer, or not entirely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coach' and 'player' suggest sport; the player is a street musician wanting loose change.
explanation.definitionFit: A coach is a long-distance road vehicle carrying many passengers, much like a large omnibus.

clue.text: He won't serve duke G&T and far odder brews!

indicators.note: brews means mixes up, so these letters are concocted into a new order

parts.note: the letters G and T of gin and tonic

explanation.surface: A waiter refuses to bring a duke his gin and tonic and some stranger drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brews' rearranges GTFARODDER after D; 'and' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who evades conscription into the armed forces refuses military service.

clue.text: Computer parts ruining the odd computer, theoretically

indicators.note: parts means splits apart, so the computer goes into the middle
odd means strange, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

parts.note: a Mac is an Apple computer

explanation.surface: Faulty computer parts are wrecking an odd machine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'odd' rearranges RUINING THE into TURINGHINE, which MAC splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Alan Turing's abstract model of computation is a computer in theory only.

clue.text: Sulphur rots mineral affected after being carried up?

parts.note: S is the chemical symbol for sulphur
addles means goes rotten, as an egg does
ore is mineral-bearing rock

explanation.surface: Chemistry: sulphur decays a mineral, which suffers after being lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: being 'carried up' by a horse leaves a rider sore.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider chafed and aching after a long time mounted on a horse is in this state.

clue.text: Greek god's drawn in line drawing

indicators.note: drawn in means pulled inside, so the line letter goes within the god's name

parts.note: Pan is the Greek god of shepherds and wild places

explanation.surface: A Greek god has been sketched in a line drawing.
explanation.definitionFit: A design or diagram, such as an architect's layout of a building, is a kind of drawing.

clue.text: Female embraced by guy in film, one with conviction?

indicators.note: embraced by says the female letter is held inside

parts.note: a male actor is a man performing in a film

explanation.surface: A woman is hugged by a film's leading man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conviction' suggests firm belief; here it is a court verdict.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer or criminal has been convicted of an offence, a pun on a person of strong beliefs.

clue.text: Arab from India on enemy ground

indicators.note: in a down-style placing, on means coming after the other piece, so the India letter goes last
ground means crushed and broken up, so the letters of enemy are rearranged

parts.note: I is India in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: An Arab soldier from India stands on enemy territory.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of the country at the south of the Arabian peninsula is an Arab.

clue.text: Half naked, did a jig, not initially subtle

indicators.note: half says only the front half of the word for naked is used

parts.note: nude means naked

indicators.note: not initially means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: to do a jig is to dance

explanation.surface: Someone half undressed performed a jig, though not very subtly.
explanation.walkthrough: NU (half of NUDE) plus ANCED (DANCED with its first letter dropped by 'not initially').
explanation.definitionFit: Something showing fine shades of meaning or distinction is subtle.

clue.text: Person selling clothing in Miami returning skirts for not fitting

indicators.note: skirts means goes round the edge of, so these letters go around the word for for
returning says the pair of pieces is read backwards

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative

indicators.note: the clothing of Miami is its outer letters

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for

explanation.surface: A salesperson dressing people in Miami heads back, skirts not fitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clothing' looks like garments, and 'skirts' too, but both are containment devices; 'for' is the piece inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Unsuitable, inappropriate behaviour is said not to be fitting.

clue.text: Note flipping sharp learner in examination

parts.note: me (or mi) is the third note of the tonic sol-fa scale

indicators.note: flipping means turned over, so the word for sharp is written backwards

parts.note: acid means sharp, as in an acid remark
L is for learner, as on a learner driver's L-plate

explanation.surface: A note about a flipping sharp student during an exam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flipping' looks like a mild British expletive, but it is the signal to turn the word round.
explanation.definitionFit: A doctor's check-up of someone's health is a physical examination.

clue.text: Judge admitting one religious offence?

indicators.note: admitting means letting in, so the one goes inside

parts.note: to judge is to decide
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A judge admits to one offence against religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Killing a god would be the ultimate sin against faith.

clue.text: Woman who's all-round crazy?

indicators.note: all-round says the word for crazy goes all round the woman

parts.note: mad means crazy
Ena is a woman's name, a crossword favourite

explanation.surface: A description of a woman who is mad in every respect.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a frenzied woman.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the frenzied female followers of Dionysus raved wildly, so one is a woman in a frenzy.

clue.text: Physique some must cover a little bit

indicators.note: must cover says the word for some goes round the other piece

parts.note: any can mean some, as in have you any
an atom is a very small bit

explanation.surface: Some modesty is needed: a body must be covered a little.
explanation.definitionFit: A person's bodily structure is their build or physique.

clue.text: Area with mostly lofty houses working without a key

indicators.note: houses means contains, so working goes inside
mostly says the last letter is dropped

parts.note: tall means lofty
on means working, operating

explanation.surface: A district of tall houses where people work without locking up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims TALL to TAL, which houses ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Music written with no tonal centre is composed without a key signature.

clue.text: Grouse seriously could be a wading bird

definitions.meaning: to grouse seriously is to complain bitterly, to protest angrily
a marsh bird related to the coot and crake

explanation.surface: A grouse, taken seriously, might be mistaken for a wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: To rail is to complain angrily, and the same word names a family of marsh birds.

clue.text: Halt cannon shot, showing composure

indicators.note: shot means wrecked or broken, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: An officer calmly orders the cannon to stop firing.
explanation.definitionFit: Being coolly calm and unconcerned is a display of composure.

clue.text: Staunch, upstanding police force succeeded

indicators.note: upstanding in a down clue means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police

explanation.surface: An honest police force has achieved success through loyalty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staunch' looks like loyal, but it is the verb meaning to stop a flow.
explanation.definitionFit: To staunch a flow of blood is to stop or check it.

clue.text: Where to find cash one's put in kitty for painter

indicators.note: put in says the first pieces go inside the word for kitty

parts.note: a kitty and a pot are both a pool of shared money
in till: the cash register in a shop
I is one, so one's is I'S

explanation.surface: An artist puts money into the shared kitty, wherever the cash comes from.
explanation.walkthrough: A till is a shop's cash register, so 'Where to find cash' reads as the phrase in till.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist who paints with small dots of pure colour, like Seurat, is a painter.

clue.text: Have time away from built-up area

indicators.note: away from means taken out of, so the time letter leaves the word for built-up area

parts.note: a town is a built-up area

explanation.surface: Someone takes a break from the city.
explanation.definitionFit: To possess something is to have it.

clue.text: Suffering around the eyes, but uncongested, we're told

indicators.note: we're told means heard rather than seen, so the word is one that sounds like spacious

parts.note: roomy means spacious, not congested

explanation.surface: Someone's eyes are sore but their sinuses are reportedly clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uncongested' seems to fit the head-cold picture, but it means spacious.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyes watery with discharge from a cold or age are said to be suffering in this way.

clue.text: Risk money, a pound, after some light shopping?

indicators.note: after places the a-and-pound pair behind the beam of light

parts.note: to bet is to risk money
a ray is a beam, some light
L is the abbreviation for pound (libra)

explanation.surface: A gambler stakes a pound after a quick bit of shopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shopping' is slang for informing on someone to the police, not buying.
explanation.definitionFit: Shopping someone, British slang for grassing to the police, is an act of treachery.
